Power 900: Evac+Chair Electric Stair Climber Chair
Product URL: https://www.anchortex.com/products/evac-chair-power-900-battery-powered-evacuation-stair-chair
Manufacturer page: https://www.evac-chair.com/evacuation-chairs/evacchair-power-900/
Spec sheet: Power 900 data sheet
Keywords (Ricky's sheet): Primary: stair climbing wheelchair (1,100/mo, KD1). Secondary: electric stair climber chair (10), evac chair 900 (0-10). Ricky's note: largest volume in the set; intent is mixed (daily care and evacuation); check the results page before committing the H1.
Recommended H1 and Subtitle
H1: Evac+Chair Electric Stair Climber Chair with 4 Speeds – Power 900
Current H1: Evac+Chair Power 900 Battery Powered Stair Chair for Daily Care and Emergency Evacuations
Subtitle: Battery Powered Stair Climbing Wheelchair Alternative with Increased Weight Capacity, for Emergency Evacuation and Daily Care
Current subtitle: Evac+Chair 1-900 Battery Powered Stair Evacuation Chair and Stair Assistance Chair for Daily Care and Evacuation Use
Revised Product Description
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
The Evac+Chair Power 900 is an electric stair climber chair that carries a seated passenger up or down the stairs with no carrying or lifting. It builds on the Power 800 with an increased weight capacity and a 4 speed control panel, so one operator can move larger passengers safely between floors during an emergency evacuation, a power outage, or daily patient transport.
It does the job many buyers look for in a stair climbing wheelchair: the passenger stays seated and strapped in while the motorized tracks do the work on the stairs. A rechargeable lithium-ion battery charges fully in 1.5 hours, and a manual stair chair mode keeps it working without power, which makes the Power 900 a good fit for care homes, hospitals, and multi-story buildings.
Operation: One person operation; motorized travel up and down the stairs, with no heavy lifting
Controls: 4 speed control panel with on/off power and ascent and descent buttons
Weight Capacity: Increased weight capacity compared with the Power 800
Battery: Rechargeable lithium-ion battery pack with burnout protection, fully charged in 1.5 hours, enough to go up and down a 5-story building 30 times
Manual Override: Manual stair chair mode when power is not available
Tracks: Automatic EVAC+TRACK release system and an adjustable stair track with a tension control system (tool included)
Passenger Safety: Extra long quick release four point harness and a height adjustable, padded orthopedic head support
Electrical Safety: Non-sparking electrical components to reduce the risk of fire
Handles: Ergonomic adjustable operator handle, plus additional operator handles for added stability when a second operator helps
Wheels: Lockable rear wheels keep the chair stationary when needed
Visibility: LED safety light for poor visibility
Frame: High strength aluminum frame
Infection Control: Wipeable materials, anti-microbial paint, and flame retardant materials
Folded Size: 19.5”W×10.6”D×45”H
Weight: 66 lbs
Certifications: FDA registered; CE and ISO 9001 certified
Compliance: Exceeds fire safety requirements and emergency response guidelines established to support the Americans with Disabilities Act
Includes: Rechargeable battery, battery charger, 2 keys, user guide, passenger headrest, passenger safety straps, photoluminescent wall sign, wall hooks, and dust cover
Warranty: Lifetime manufacturer’s warranty
Design: Designed in the United States
Available Models and Options
Power 900 – Electric Stair Climber Chair: 4 speeds, increased weight capacity, up and down the stairs
[H2] Applications
The Power 900 suits buildings that need to move larger passengers on the stairs, both in an emergency and day to day.
Typical applications include:
Care homes, nursing homes, and assisted living facilities
Emergency evacuation and power outages in hospitals and multi-story buildings, when the elevators cannot be used
Daily patient transport between floors
Schools, offices, hotels, and high-rise buildings
Explore Anchortex's Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers collection for more evacuation equipment.
[H2] Frequently Asked Questions
Is the Power 900 a stair climbing wheelchair?
It does the same job on the stairs: the passenger stays seated and strapped in while the motorized tracks carry them up or down. It is a folding stair chair, not an everyday wheelchair, so it is used for moving between floors.
How is the Power 900 different from the Power 800?
The Power 900 has an increased weight capacity, 4 speed settings, an automatic EVAC+TRACK release system, and a lifetime manufacturer's warranty.
How long does the battery last?
The lithium-ion battery charges fully in 1.5 hours, which is enough to go up and down a 5-story building 30 times.
Can it be used without power?
Yes. The manual stair chair mode lets the operator use the Power 900 as a manual stair chair when the battery is not available.
[H2] About Evac+Chair Evacuation Chairs
Evac+Chair makes stair evacuation chairs, powered stair chairs, evacuation sleds, and accessories for moving people with limited mobility on stairs, in an emergency or every day.
The Evac+Chair line includes:
Emergency evacuation chairs: The 300H, 400H, 600H, and 750H stair evacuation chairs for controlled travel down the stairs
Powered stair climbing chairs: The battery powered Power 800 and Power 900 for going up and down the stairs
Stair transport seat: The IBEX 700H Tran-Seat for two-person transport up and down the stairs
Evacuation sleds and mats: The Evac+Sled, Ulti-Mat, and Evac+Sheet rescue sheet
Accessories: Comfy Seat, transfer seat, storage cabinets, anti-theft alarms, and the iEvac smoke and fire escape hood
[H2] About Evac+Chair
Evac+Chair has made stairway evacuation chairs since 1982, and its chairs were designed in the United States. Explore the full line of Evac+Chair evacuation chairs at Anchortex.

Notes and Questions
Keywords and H1: Ricky asked to check the results page before using "stair climbing wheelchair" in the H1. The results for that term are research projects, patents, and news about wheelchairs that climb stairs on their own, not product pages for stair chairs. So I used "electric stair climber chair" (Evac+Chair's own wording) in the H1, and put "stair climbing wheelchair" in the subtitle, intro, a FAQ, and the meta description. If you prefer it in the H1: "Evac+Chair Power 900 Stair Climbing Wheelchair – Battery Powered Stair Chair".
"Stair climbing chair" is the Power 800 page's primary keyword, so I did not use it here, to keep the two pages from competing.
WEIGHT CAPACITY: our page and the Evac+Chair web page say 560 lbs, but the Power 900 data sheet says 500 lbs (and the Evac+Chair home page says "up to 500lbs"). I wrote "increased weight capacity" until you confirm the number.
Speeds: our page and the Evac+Chair web page say 4 speeds. The data sheet text is unclear. I used 4 speeds.
Warranty: the Evac+Chair web page and data sheet both say lifetime manufacturer's warranty for the Power 900 (unlike the Power 800).
Name: our subtitle says "1-900". Evac+Chair calls it the Power 900, so I used Power 900.
Shipping weight: the variant is set to 200 lbs. The chair weighs 66 lbs. Is 200 lbs the boxed weight?
Price: $3,795 with compare-at $5,060 (75%, not 80%). No change made.
Added from the Evac+Chair page and data sheet: automatic EVAC+TRACK release system, non-sparking electrical components, battery burnout protection, LED safety light, and "Designed in the United States."
Current meta description is a general GSA pricing line. Is GSA pricing still offered?
FAQs: added 4, including "Is the Power 900 a stair climbing wheelchair?" to answer the search term honestly.
Images: the page has only one image. Would you like me to add Power 900 photos from the Evac+Chair website?
